Raymond III was the count of Tripoli from 1152 to 1187. He was born around 1140 to Raymond II and Hodierna of Jerusalem. His father died when he was young and his mother acted as regent until he came of age. He inherited a county that lay between the Kingdom of Jerusalem and the Principality of Antioch. The county was a vassal of Jerusalem but also maintained ties with Antioch and Byzantium.

*Early Life* Raymond III spent his youth at the court of Jerusalem where he learned the art of warfare and diplomacy. He married Eschiva of Bures in 1160 which strengthened his links with the local nobility. The marriage produced several children including his successor Raymond IV. He also cultivated relationships with the Knights Templar and the Hospitallers who held important castles in his territory.

*Reign and Politics* During his rule Raymond III pursued a policy of balancing power among the Crusader states. He often allied with the King of Jerusalem against Muslim threats but he also negotiated with Nur ad Din and later Saladin when it suited his interests. In 1164 he helped defend the frontier against Nur ad Din's raids. He participated in the failed expedition to Egypt in 1169 which aimed to weaken Saladin's growing power. Raymond III also dealt with internal disputes among his vassals and worked to secure the succession of his son.

*Later Years and Death* By the early 1180s Saladin had united much of Syria and Egypt under his rule. Raymond III saw the growing danger and tried to forge a coalition with other Christian leaders. In 1187 after the disastrous Battle of Hattin he was captured by Saladin's forces. He was released after a short captivity but his health declined rapidly. He died in 1187 shortly after his release and was buried in Tripoli. His death marked the end of an independent Tripoli as the county fell under direct Crusader royal control.
